entities.summary:
Antonio Trivulzio the Elder (1457–1508) was an Italian Roman Catholic bishop and cardinal. He was born in 1457, but his exact birthdate is unknown. Trivulzio served as bishop of Como from 1484 until his death in 1508. During his tenure, he played a key role in the Italian Wars, supporting the French king Louis XII. Trivulzio's papal legations took him to Rome, where he participated in the politics of the Vatican. He was a strong advocate for the interests of the Church and worked closely with other cardinals to shape the Church's policy. Trivulzio's diplomatic efforts were instrumental in securing a favorable treaty between France and the Papal States. His legacy as a skilled diplomat and administrator has endured for centuries, with many historians praising his ability to navigate the complex web of alliances and rivalries that defined the Italian Renaissance. Trivulzio's impact on the Church can still be seen in the many buildings and institutions he helped establish during his papal legations.

Trivulzio's contributions to the Church were significant, but his legacy extends beyond the realm of religion. He was a shrewd politician who recognized the importance of maintaining good relations with secular powers. His diplomatic efforts helped to maintain stability in Italy, which was a crucial factor in the continent's ability to recover from the devastation of the Black Death. Trivulzio's experience as a diplomat also gave him a deep understanding of the complexities of international relations, which he applied to his role as a cardinal. This expertise helped to shape the Church's foreign policy and ensure its continued relevance in the centuries that followed.
